verifications.claim: NASA successfully launched the Artemis II mission on April 1, 2026, at 6:35 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'lifting off at 6.35pm ... 1 Apr 2026'; R3: 'blasted off ... at 6:35 p.m. Eastern time'; R4: 'lifted off ... at 6:35 p.m. EDT'; R8: 'lifted off ... at 6:35 p.m. EDT Wednesday'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm the exact date, time, and successful launch.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission sent four astronauts on a 10-day, 695,000-mile journey around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '10-day lunar flyby'; R3: 'round trip of more than 695,000 miles'; R4: 'nearly 700,000-mile trip'; R5: 'nearly 700,000-mile'; R7: 'nearly 700,000-mile'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm 10-day mission around the Moon with four astronauts and matching mileage (exact or very close).

verifications.claim: The crew of the Artemis II mission consists of NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman (commander), Victor Glover (pilot), Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover and Christina Koch, plus Jeremy Hansen from the Canadian Space Agency'; R2/R4/R6/R7/R8/R9: identical crew listing with roles
verifications.reasoning: All sources consistently list the exact crew with roles.

verifications.claim: The launch vehicle for the Artemis II mission is the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Space Launch System'; R2/R4/R6/R8/R9: 'SLS (Space Launch System) rocket'

verifications.claim: The spacecraft for the Artemis II mission is the Orion capsule named Integrity.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'spacecraft named Integrity'; R4: 'Orion, named Integrity'; R5: 'Orion capsule, Integrity'; R8: 'Orion, which the crew named “Integrity”'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly name the Orion capsule as Integrity.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed flight test of the SLS and Orion systems.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'testing its systems for the first time with astronauts'; R6: 'first time a Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion spacecraft have carried astronauts'; R7: 'first time that NASA’s Space Launch System rocket and Orion capsule carry human passengers'; R8: 'first crewed flight of this rocket and spacecraft'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm it as the first crewed test of SLS and Orion.

verifications.claim: Artemis II travels further from Earth than any human since Apollo 17 in 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'farther from Earth than any human being before them'; R3: '252,799 miles ... farther than the Apollo 13'; R6: 'farther from Earth than any humans in history ... farther than ... Apollo 13'; R7: 'surpassing the Apollo 13 distance record ... set in 1970'
verifications.reasoning: Sources state it exceeds previous records (Apollo 13, post-Apollo 17 no deep space travel), and no humans beyond LEO since Apollo 17.

verifications.claim: The crew of Artemis II will perform systems tests, including life support checks, to prepare for future lunar surface missions Artemis III and IV.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'test flight designed to evaluate the Orion crew capsule and essential life support ... ahead of future Artemis missions, including ... Artemis IV'; R3: 'check that the spacecraft can safely make the journey and keep its crew alive'; R8: 'demonstrate life support systems ... lay the foundation for ... Moon ahead of future missions'
verifications.reasoning: Direct support for systems/life support tests preparing future missions including III/IV; slightly vague on exact missions but context matches.

verifications.claim: Christina Koch is the first woman on a lunar mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first woman ... to fly into cislunar space'; R3: 'first woman to do so [venture into deep space]'; R6: 'first woman ... to the moon'; R7: 'first woman ... on a lunar mission'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly stated as first woman on lunar/deep space mission.

verifications.claim: Victor Glover is the first person of color on a lunar mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first person of color to fly into cislunar space'; R3: 'first Black man to venture into deep space'; R6/R7: 'first person of color ... on a lunar mission'

verifications.claim: Jeremy Hansen is the first non-U.S. citizen on a lunar mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'first person on a moon mission who is not an American'; R6: 'first non-American to the moon'; R7: 'first Canadian on a lunar mission'

verifications.claim: The crew of Artemis II is scheduled to splash down in the Pacific Ocean after completing their lunar flyby.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splashdown in the Pacific Ocean'; R3: 'splashdown in the Pacific Ocean on April 10'; R5: 'splashdown ... into the Pacific'; R8: 'splash down in the Pacific Ocean'
